title: Colon-targeted EGCG delivery remodels the gut microenvironment to enhance therapeutic efficacy in ulcerative colitis.
abstract: Ulcerative colitis (UC) is a chronic intestinal inflammatory disorder characterized by epithelial barrier disruption, oxidative stress, and gut microbiota dysbiosis. Although epigallocatechin-3-gallate (EGCG) exhibits potent anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activities, its clinical application is limited by poor stability and low colonic bioavailability. Herein, EGCG-loaded Eudragit® S100-coated chitosan microparticles (EG@euCS MPs) were developed as a colon-targeted oral delivery platforms int

title: Akkermansia muciniphila attenuates anti-tuberculosis drug-induced liver injury through gut-liver axis by promoting Nr4a1 transcription.
abstract: Drug-induced liver injury (DILI) is a frequent adverse event associated with anti-tuberculosis therapy, and current clinical management options remain limited. Given the pivotal role of the gut-liver axis in liver pathophysiology, this study investigated the potential and underlying roles of Akkermansia muciniphila (A.muc) in ameliorating anti-tuberculosis drug-induced liver injury (ADLI). title: Lactobacillus-Based Therapy for Ulcerative Colitis: From Strain Heterogeneity and TCM-Mediated Modulation to Engineered Delivery and Precision Translation.
abstract: Although Lactobacillus sensu lato is widely considered a promising microecological intervention for ulcerative colitis, its clinical translation remains severely constrained by strain-specific efficacy, host microenvironmental dependency, and the risk of opportunistic systemic translocation across a compromised intestinal barrier. The historical assumption of genus-level therapeutic uniformity is increasingly inadequate, as even closely related strains can exhibit divergent or occasionally adver

title: Hybrid genome assemblies of Bacteroidota isolates uncover mobile genetic elements, antimicrobial resistance genes, and novel antimicrobial peptides.
abstract: Members of the phylum Bacteroidota dominate the mammalian gut microbiota and represent promising candidates for next-generation probiotics. However, the resolution of complete Bacteroidota genomes is often hindered by extensive repetitive sequences and mobile genetic elements, a technical challenge further exacerbated by high intraspecies diversity and strain-level variants that drive assembly fragmentation and preclude the recovery of contiguous scaffolds. title: An antibiotic-treated mouse model reveals the progression of intestinal botulism.
abstract: Intestinal botulism, including infant botulism and adult intestinal toxemia botulism, is a life-threatening disease caused by intestinal infection with Clostridium botulinum (Cb) spores. Infants are particularly susceptible to Cb infection because of their immature gut microbiota, whereas healthy adults are generally protected by gut microbiota-mediated colonization resistance. Thus, immature gut microbiota or gut dysbiosis is thought to permit Cb colonization. However, the mechanisms underlying

title: Sodium Butyrate: A Microbiota-Derived Short-Chain Fatty Acid Regulating Inflammation, Gut Barrier Function, and Colorectal Cancer Progression.
abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is a polyetiologic disease related to genetic changes, chronic inflammation, dysregulation of the intestinal barrier, diet and gut microbiota dysbiosis. Butyrate is a short-chain fatty acid (SCFA) produced by the microbiota that plays a crucial role in energy metabolism, epithelial homeostasis and mucosal immunity. title: Allicin attenuates diet-induced obesity in association with gut microbiota remodeling, fecal butyrate, and hepatic PPAR signaling in rats.
abstract: Obesity is associated with gut microbial dysbiosis and impaired intestinal barrier function. Allicin, a garlic-derived organosulfur compound, has shown anti-obesity effects, but the links between its effects on gut microbial metabolism and hepatic gene expression remain unclear. This study examined the metabolic effects of allicin and associated gut-liver responses using microbiota profiling, targeted short-chain fatty acid (SCFA) metabolomics, hepatic transcriptomics, network pharmacology and q

title: Microbiome-associated metabolites as emerging biomarkers of cancer immunotherapy response: from mechanistic networks to clinical validation.
abstract: Immune checkpoint blockade has improved outcomes across several cancers, yet many patients experience primary or acquired resistance. The gut microbiome may contribute to this variation through metabolic activities that influence systemic and tumor-associated immunity. This narrative review examines microbiome-associated metabolites as potential markers of immunotherapy response, with particular attention to their biological origins, immune effects, and clinical validation. title: Postbiotics derived from Latilactobacillus curvatus alleviate alcoholic liver injury by reshaping intestinal microbiota and activating the lysozyme-AHR-IL-22 axis.
abstract: Long-term alcohol exposure disrupts gut microbiota and mucosal immune homeostasis, promoting the pathogenesis of alcohol-associated liver disease (ALD) via the gut-liver axis. Postbiotic intervention has emerged as a potential strategy for alleviating ALD, yet its protective mechanisms within the impaired intestinal microenvironment remain unclear. This study investigated whether postbiotics derived from Latilactobacillus curvatus can alleviate alcohol-associated liver disease (ALD) and explored

title: Microbiota-dependent biofunctionality of sulfated fucans from Saccharina japonica during intestinal epithelial development in juvenile mice: Limosilactobacillus reuteri L11 as a microbial responder.
abstract: Previous studies have demonstrated that sulfated fucans from Saccharina japonica (SJ-FUC) promote intestinal epithelial development in juvenile mice. However, whether this biofunctionality depends on the gut microbiota and which microbial responders contribute to this process remain unclear. title: Multi-omics studies show that naringin improves cyclophosphamide-induced testicular and intestinal damage by enhancing energy metabolism.
abstract: Cyclophosphamide (CTX) is an anticancer agent that severely impairs male reproductive health. Naringin (NAR), a flavonoid compound, has the potential to ameliorate CTX-induced damage; however, the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. In this study, an integrative approach combining transcriptomics, microbiome analysis, and serum metabolomics was employed to comprehensively evaluate the protective effects of NAR on reproductive function in CTX-treated mice. title: Temporal and Spatial Dynamics and Mechanisms of Brain-Gut Axis Injury Induced by Confinement-Like Physical Restraint Stress in Mice.
abstract: Long-term SIS exposure across aerospace, deep-sea, underground, and quarantine settings increases depression and gut-brain axis dysfunction risk, but long-term nonlinear injury dynamics remain poorly understood.

title: Association of Blastocystis with the gut bacteria abundance and serum levels of serotonin in patients with irritable bowel syndrome; a case-control study.
abstract: Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) is a chronic disorder of gut-brain axis. Although Blastocystis colonization has been reported in patients with IBS, the role of this parasite in modulation of the gut microbiota composition and the serotonin levels remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate association of Blastocystis colonization with serotonin-pathway-associated bacteria and serotonin levels in patients with IBS and healthy individuals. title: Beyond the brain: curcumin as a multi-target neuropharmacological modulator of the gut-brain axis in major depressive disorder and Parkinson's disease.
abstract: Curcumin, the principal polyphenol of Curcuma longa, has been proposed as a multi-target neuropharmacological agent for neuropsychiatric and neurodegenerative disorders. We propose that major depressive disorder (MDD) and Parkinson's disease (PD) share a convergent gut-brain axis dysfunction, and that curcumin can serve as a pharmacological probe to test whether this convergent pathway is causally relevant. title: Immunometabolic and epigenetic reprogramming in inflammatory bowel disease: from mechanistic circuits to therapeutic targeting.
abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is a chronic, immune-mediated disorder of the gastrointestinal tract and an escalating global public health challenge, particularly in newly industrializing regions. Its etiology and pathogenesis remain incompletely understood, although disrupted homeostasis between the intestinal microbiota and the mucosal immune system is implicated. title: Children at risk of vitamin A deficiency exhibit taxonomic dysbiosis and functional remodeling of the gut microbiome: a matched case-control study.
abstract: Vitamin A deficiency is one of the most prevalent micronutrient deficiencies worldwide. This condition increases susceptibility to infections and due to its role in intestinal barrier integrity, it has been suggested that it could predispose to gut dysbiosis.

title: The (amide-)N-methylnicotinamide is a microbe-derived NAD+ precursor that drives gut stem cell renewal.
abstract: Nicotinamide Adenine Dinucleotide (NAD) is a critical cellular coenzyme whose decline associates with various chronic and inflammatory diseases. Improved NAD restoration may reduce disease risks and extend healthy lifespan. We report here that certain commensal bacteria including specific probiotic species produce (amide-)N-methylnicotinamide (N-MNA), which is a structural isomer of methylnicotinamide, a nicotinamide degradative metabolite. title: Study on Reconstruction of Functional Lactic Acid Bacteria Communities and on the Lipid Lowering Effect of their Fermented Lotus Leaf Beverage.
abstract: Hyperlipidemia, caused by dysregulated lipid metabolism, is closely associated with cardiovascular risk. This study developed a lipid-lowering beverage by fermenting lotus leaf (Nelumbo nucifera) extract with functional lactic acid bacteria (LAB). Three strains, Lactobacillus paracasei GY-L077, Lactiplantibacillus plantarum GY-L085, and Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus RB-01, were selected from traditional fermented foods for their antibacterial activity, gamma-aminobutyric acid production, lipase p

title: Comparative evaluation of edible Bifidobacterium species in repairing 5-fluorouracil induced intestinal microenvironment damage.
abstract: Chemotherapy-induced disruption of the intestinal microenvironment severely compromises both the quality of life and clinical prognosis of cancer patients. Despite the potential of edible Bifidobacterium to alleviate chemotherapy-associated intestinal damage, substantial inter-species comparisons remain to be clarified to support the rational selection of probiotic candidates. title: Effects of low-dose atorvastatin combined with reduced-dose prednisolone in acetic acid-induced ulcerative colitis in rats.
abstract: Long-term corticosteroid treatment for ulcerative colitis (UC) is often limited by dose-dependent adverse effects, highlighting the need for strategies that reduce steroid exposure. This study evaluated the efficacy of a combination of half-doses of Atorvastatin and Prednisolone in rats with acetic acid-induced colitis. title: High-carbohydrate and low-carbohydrate diets enriched in type II resistant starch from high-amylose maize influence cholesterol metabolism via concurrent alterations in fecal Bifidobacterium pseudolongum, bile salt hydrolase and bile acid profiles in mice.
abstract: This study investigated the impacts of high-carbohydrate (HC) and low-carbohydrate (LC) diets enriched in type II resistant starch from high-amylose maize (HAM-RS2) on circulating cholesterol concentrations and mechanisms linked to gut microbiota and bile acids. Compared to corn starch, HAM-RS2 resulted in lower plasma TC, LDL-C, and VLDL-C concentrations and adiposity, particularly in an HC context. title: Secondary bile acids disrupt hematopoietic stem cell homeostasis.
abstract: Gut microbiota dysbiosis caused by a high-fat diet disrupts hematopoietic stem cell (HSC) homeostasis; however, the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Here, we identify gut microbial secondary bile acid deoxycholic acid (DCA) as a key mediator of HSC dysfunction in mice. Plasma DCA levels were elevated during aging, consistent with previously reported increases in high-fat diet-fed mice. title: Fecal microbiome and plasma metabolome responses to Bacillus-based direct-fed microbial supplementation in cow-calf pairs from late gestation through weaning.
abstract: This study evaluated the effects of supplementation of a Bacillus-based direct-fed microbial (DFM) on the plasma metabolome and fecal microbiome of multiparous beef cow-calf pairs. On day 0 (94 ± 19 days prepartum), 296 Brangus crossbred beef cows were randomly assigned to treatments consisting of free-choice access to a trace mineral supplement alone (CON) or combined (BAC) with Bacillus subtilis 810 and B. licheniformis 809 (3 g/head/day; 6.6 × 109 CFU/head/day) from day 0 to 330 (weaning). title: Heat-inactivated Bifidobacterium adolescentis LA20 alleviates doxorubicin-induced senescence and barrier dysfunction in feline intestinal epithelial cells.
abstract: To investigate the protective effects and molecular mechanisms of heat-inactivated Bifidobacterium adolescentis LA-20 (HT-LA20) against doxorubicin (DOX)-induced senescent injury in feline intestinal epithelial cells (FIECs).

title: Hypoxia orchestrates the natural history of inflammatory bowel disease: Mechanisms and therapeutic opportunities.
abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) arises from a dynamic interplay between epithelial dysfunction, immune activation, microbial dysbiosis and tissue remodelling. Although hypoxia was initially regarded as a consequence of intestinal inflammation, it is now recognized as an active regulator of epithelial, immune and stromal responses that coordinate disease progression. title: Microbial depolymerization of Siegesbeckia orientalis polysaccharide suggests a potential cross-feeding mechanism underlying the enrichment of Limosilactobacillus reuteri SOP-1 in the gut.
abstract: Plant polysaccharides are structurally complex biological macromolecules whose biological functions may depend on their microbial transformation in the gut. However, how microbial depolymerization of dietary polysaccharides influences subsequent microbial interactions remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated the microbial utilization and biological functions of polysaccharides derived from the Chinese medicinal herb Siegesbeckia orientalis L. (SOP) in high-fat diet-fed mice. title: Effects of Lactobacillus crispatus-Containing Probiotics and Metformin on Insulin Resistance, Inflammation, and Gut Microbiome in Polycystic Ovary Syndrome: Protocol for an Open-Label Randomized Controlled Trial.
abstract: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) affects 9% to 12% of reproductive-age women worldwide, with higher prevalence reported in India. Its pathophysiology involves insulin resistance, hyperandrogenism, and chronic low-grade inflammation, increasingly linked to gut dysbiosis and lipopolysaccharide-driven toll-like receptor 4 signaling. title: Lactobacillus Plantarum-Derived Extracellular Vesicles Alleviate DSS-Induced Colitis and Modulate Autophagy-Related Markers.
abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) encompasses a group of chronic inflammatory disorders of the intestine, which have been associated with a rising global incidence. Autophagy plays a crucial anti-inflammatory role in the context of intestinal inflammation. title: Targeting hormone conversion through dietary fiber improves polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome.
abstract: Excessive androgens serve as a primary driver for many phenotypic features of polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS). Although dietary fiber has been shown to alleviate PMOS, its effects on androgen concentrations and the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. In a clinical trial, we demonstrated that a dietary fiber combination consisting of inulin, resistant starch, and β-glucan reduces androgen concentrations in patients' plasma. title: Microbial metabolism of methotrexate produces a STAT3 signaling molecule that alleviates gut inflammation.
abstract: Methotrexate (MTX) is a gold standard therapy for inflammatory diseases but has mixed therapeutic success in inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). The gut microbiota impact MTX efficacy and toxicity by metabolizing MTX and altering its bioavailability, yet how inflammation alters this metabolism, and how the resulting metabolites act on the host, remain poorly understood. title: Chronic Arsenic Exposure Induces Hepatocyte Proliferation in Rats via the Gut-Liver Axis: Interventions With Fecal Microbiota Transplantation and/or Arsenic Withdrawal.
abstract: Arsenic (As) contamination in groundwater has been reported in many countries and is a major risk factor for liver injury. While the impact of arsenic exposure on gut microbiota and its role in liver diseases through the gut-liver axis has been documented, the underlying mechanism remains unclear. In this study, we established a chronic arsenic exposure rat model by administering sodium arsenite (NaAsO2) at concentrations of 30 and 100 mg/L through drinking water until 62 weeks of age. title: Optimized Super-SILAC Normalization Enables Enhanced Profiling of Histone Post-Translational Modification Changes Associated with Microbiota and Acute Inflammation.
abstract: The gut microbiota produces metabolites, such as short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) that modulate histone acylation and serve as precursors for non-acetyl acyl marks, representing a mechanism in host-microbiome epigenetic crosstalk. However, the reliable quantification of these low-abundance modifications in complex tissues remains challenging. title: Bioaccessibility and Microbial Metabolism of (Poly)phenol-Rich Dietary Fiber Fractions from Frozen Mixed Berries in an In Vitro Model.
abstract: Berries are rich in (poly)phenols and dietary fiber (DF), both known for their health-promoting properties. However, little is known about how these compounds interact within the berry matrix. This study characterized berry fiber fractions as value-added ingredients and assessed their effects on (poly)phenol bioaccessibility and fecal microbiota metabolism. title: Longitudinal associations of the gut microbiome with arterial stiffness in US adults: findings from the Baltimore Longitudinal Study of Aging.
abstract: The gut microbiome affects arterial stiffness in experimental murine models; however, evidence in human longitudinal studies is lacking. In this study, we investigated longitudinal between-person (average) and within-person (change) associations of microbiome features with arterial stiffness. We assessed the fecal microbiome using whole genome metagenomic sequencing, and arterial stiffness using carotid-femoral pulse wave velocity (cfPWV). title: Propionyl-Fructooligosaccharide Alleviates DSS-Induced Colitis in Association with Changes in Gut Microbiota, Inflammatory Responses, and Intestinal Barrier Function.
abstract: Propionyl-fructooligosaccharide (P-FOS), an esterified prebiotic synthesized from fructooligosaccharides and propionic acid, was evaluated in a dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)-induced colitis mouse model. P-FOS treatment was associated with lower disease activity, attenuated colon shortening, reduced histological injury, and the preservation of goblet cells. title: Allobaculum stercoricanis and Its Postbiotics Alleviate Dextran Sulfate Sodium (DSS)-Induced Colitis through the Regulation of theTLR4/NF-κB Signaling Pathway.
abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is a chronic intestinal disorder that has become a global public health concern. Postbiotics offer advantages in biosafety and reproducibility over probiotics. Here, we demonstrated that live Allobaculum stercoricanis (A. stercoricanis) and its two postbiotic preparations─inactivated bacterial cells (POST) and cell-free fermentation supernatant (CFS)─effectively alleviated dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)-induced colitis in mice. title: Food-Grade Silicon Dioxide Nanoparticles Disrupt the Microbiota-Associated Gut-Liver Axis and FXR-Related Bile Acid Homeostasis in Mice.
abstract: Food-grade silica (E551) is widely used as an anticaking additive, raising concerns about repeated exposure to nanoscale silica fractions. However, its long-term effects on microbiota-associated gut-liver regulation and FXR-related bile acid homeostasis remain unclear. Male C57BL/6J mice were fed control or SiO2NP-containing diets providing 225, 1000, or 5000 mg/kg bw/day for 8 weeks. journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry

title: Rethinking Pathogenesis of Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis.
abstract: Primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) is a chronic cholestatic liver disease characterized by progressive fibroinflammatory injury of intrahepatic and extrahepatic bile ducts that may lead to cirrhosis, hepatobiliary malignancy, and death, with liver transplantation representing the only effective intervention in end-stage disease. title: Arabinoxylan Enhances Intestinal Mucosal Barrier Function and Antioxidant Capacity in Suckling Piglet Associated with Remodeled Gut Microbiota and Upregulated AHR-Related Signaling.
abstract: Milk replacers are essential when breastfeeding is limited, but strategies for incorporating functional polysaccharides to support neonatal intestinal development remain unclear. Here, suckling piglets were used as a model to investigate the effects of arabinoxylan (AX) supplementation in a milk replacer on growth, intestinal function, and microbiota-related metabolism. title: Inulin Combined with Rosmarinic Acid Alleviates D-Galactose-Induced Cognitive Impairment by Regulating Indoxyl Sulfate and the AhR/NF-κB/NLRP3 Inflammatory Pathway.
abstract: Age-related cognitive impairment is associated with oxidative stress, intestinal barrier dysfunction, and gut-brain axis disruption. This study evaluated how rosmarinic acid (RA), alone or combined with the prebiotic inulin, ameliorates D-galactose-induced cognitive impairment in mice. Male ICR mice received D-galactose for 6 weeks with RA, or RA plus inulin, followed by behavioral testing, histology, biochemical assays, 16S rRNA sequencing, serum metabolomics, molecular dynamics and inflammator
journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry

title: Probiotics for Human Health: Mechanisms, Clinical Evidence, Risks, and Next-Generation Microbial Therapeutics.
abstract: Probiotics are widely used live microbial supplements intended to promote human health, yet their clinical benefits remain inconsistent and often strain-specific. Most currently available probiotics are derived from Lactobacillus, Bifidobacterium, and Saccharomyces species originally isolated from fermented foods or human microbiota. title: Panax notoginseng alleviates obesity and insulin resistance involving the Enterocloster clostridioformis-IRS-PI3K-AKT axis.
abstract: In this study, supplementation with Panax notoginseng (PN) in obese mice reversed excessive weight gain, improved glucose homeostasis and insulin sensitivity, and significantly reversed hepatic steatosis. Concurrently, PN treatment normalized the intestinal microecosystem, reflected in a decreased Firmicutes-to-Bacteroidetes ratio (F/B ratio) and an enrichment of the commensal species Enterocloster clostridioformis (EC). title: Gut Microbiota-Derived β-Glucuronidase Governs the Anticolitic Efficacy of Daidzein via the ERβ-PI3K/Akt/mTOR-Autophagy Axis.
abstract: Precision nutritional interventions targeting the gut microenvironment have emerged as a pivotal strategy for managing inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). However, the specific microbial mechanisms governing the therapeutic efficacy of dietary flavonoids, such as daidzein (DA), remain largely unexplored. In this study, it was observed that administration of 40 mg/kg DA significantly attenuated DSS-induced colitis, preserving mucosal barrier integrity and suppressing inflammation. Multiomics analys
journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry

title: DC vaccine loaded with Bacteroides fragilis elicits functional cross-reactivity and enhances anti-PD-1 immunotherapy.
abstract: The gut microbiome profoundly influences the clinical benefits of antitumor immunotherapy. Although various gut microbiota have been shown to enhance immunotherapy, their clinical application remains unexplored. In this study, a dendritic cell (DC) vaccine loaded with the gut commensal Bacteroides fragilis (DC-Bf) was used as a therapeutic cancer vaccine. title: Engineering commensal Lachnospiraceae for programmable therapeutic delivery in the mouse gut.
abstract: Engineered native gut bacteria could offer persistent, programmable therapeutic delivery in the gut, but many dominant taxa remain genetically intractable. Members of one such family of obligate anaerobic Clostridia, Lachnospiraceae, are prevalent in the human gut microbiome and produce metabolites linked to intestinal and metabolic health. title: Oral Protein Fibril Microgels with Gastric Stability and Intestinal Targeting Enhance Capsaicin Bioavailability for Effective Obesity Prevention.
abstract: To address the susceptibility of protein fibrils to pepsin degradation, this study proposed a fibril-to-microgel hierarchical assembly strategy, where flexible whey protein isolate fibrils (WPIF) and rigid flaxseed protein isolate fibrils (FPIF) were in situ self-cross-linked into microgels via a W/O emulsion template, followed by capsaicin (Cap) loading. journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry

title: Engineered Chiral Probiotics Ameliorate MASH via Gut-Liver Axis.
abstract: The global epidemic of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) is escalating without effective therapies. This study identified a significant depletion of the gut commensal bacterium Faecalibacterium duncaniae (F. duncaniae) as a core feature of MASH. To overcome the poor colonization by traditional probiotics in inflammatory environments, we engineered a living microbial therapeutic by incorporating chiral gold nanozymes onto F. duncaniae. title: Impact of arsenic exposure on the gut-microbiota-liver axis in poultry.
abstract: Arsenic (As), a priority hazardous substance widely distributed in nature, endangers poultry health and food safety. The gut‑microbiota‑liver axis forms a bidirectional regulatory network, with the intestine acting as the main absorption site and the liver as the key metabolic‑detoxification organ for As. title: Core microbial populations drive longitudinal development of the hindgut bacterial microbiota in Jersey calves.
abstract: The early-life gut microbiome represents a critical window during which microbial succession may exert lasting effects on host metabolism and productivity. While gut microbiome-host phenotypic associations have been extensively studied in Holstein calves, such relationships are rarely reported in alternative breeds, including Jersey calves. title: Microbiota-derived metabolite-GPCR signalling in neurodegeneration.
abstract: The gut microbiome acts as a primary regulator of host homeostasis, influencing the entire body through bidirectional communication along the gut-brain axis (GBA). Dysbiosis, which is defined as a state of microbial imbalance involving alterations in community composition and function, can disrupt the synthesis of important microbiota-derived metabolites, such as short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), bile acids and neurotransmitter precursors. title: Gain and loss of acquired doxycycline resistance in Lactiplantibacillus plantarum: an adaptive laboratory evolution study.
abstract: Probiotics interact in a mutualistic way with humans. Exposure of probiotics to sublethal concentrations of commonly prescribed antibiotics can cause resistance to arise. Over 1,000 generations, we performed an adaptive laboratory evolution experiment to determine if the fitness of the probiotic Lactiplantibacillus plantarum is altered by exposure to doxycycline (DOX) at one-tenth of the minimal inhibitory concentration. title: Heterogeneity of microbiome responses to menopausal hormone therapy among perimenopausal women.
abstract: Menopausal hormone therapy (MHT) alleviates climacteric symptoms, yet its microbiome-wide effects and efficacy determinants remain unclear. Here we show that oral estradiol/dydrogesterone, given for 6 months to 356 perimenopausal women, improved neuroendocrine, metabolic and symptom outcomes and induced site-specific microbial remodeling. title: Lactiplantibacillus plantarum Lp05 ensures immune developmental safety and protects against colitis via promoting Treg differentiation in mice.
abstract: Lactiplantibacillus plantarum (formerly Lactobacillus plantarum) Lp05, a strain isolated from pickled vegetables, is widely used as a probiotic in the food industry. However, its impact on the host immune system, especially the adaptive immune system, remains poorly understood. In this study, we systematically evaluated the influence of Lp05 on T cell immunity under both homeostatic and inflammatory conditions in mice. title: Systemically delivered Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron-derived bacterial extracellular vesicles inhibit primary and metastatic melanoma growth.
abstract: The gut microbiome can contribute to anti-tumor immunity and cancer therapy responses, but translating live microbe-based interventions remains challenging due to safety, controllability, and delivery constraints. Bacterial extracellular vesicles (BEVs) are an attractive cell-free alternative, as they package bacterial cargo into a nanoscale format capable of host-cell engagement, immunological activation, and systemic distribution. title: Characterization of a Unique Carbohydrate-Binding Module from Akkermansia muciniphila that Binds Ganglioside-Associated Glycans.
abstract: Akkermansia muciniphila is a mucin-degrading gut symbiont that promotes host metabolic health through its ability to utilize host-derived glycans. Central to this microbe is its diverse set of glycoside hydrolases (GHs), specifically GHs involved in degrading host glycans like mucin. Here, we characterize an A. muciniphila GH from family 123 (AmGH123), that has β-N-acetyl-d-galactosaminidase activity, removing terminal β-linked GalNAc from ganglioside-associated glycans similar to other GH123s.

title: Dual Gut Microbiota-Dependent Mechanisms Underlying the Anti-Atherosclerotic Effect of Tilianin.
abstract: Tilianin (Til), a flavonoid from Dracocephalum moldavica L. and Agastache species, exerts potent anti-atherosclerotic effects via gut microbiota-mediated mechanisms. In atherosclerotic mice, Til dose-dependently reduced plaque burden and enhanced plaque stability by reducing necrotic cores and increasing collagen. title: Microbiota-derived indole-3-propionic acid regulates glucose homeostasis via remodeling of hepatic mitochondrial metabolism.
abstract: The gut microbiota produces metabolites that circulate to host tissues and are increasingly linked to metabolic health, yet the mechanisms by which individual microbial products regulate liver glucose metabolism remain poorly defined. Here, we identify the tryptophan-derived microbial metabolite indole-3-propionic acid (IPA) as a direct modulator of hepatic glucose production. title: β-glucan mitigates necrotizing enterocolitis-induced long-term cognitive impairment by remodeling gut microbiota and restoring tryptophan metabolite IAA-mediated gut-brain signaling.
abstract: Necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) is a life-threatening gastrointestinal disorder prevalent in preterm infants, and most NEC survivors suffer from persistent cognitive deficits and neurodevelopmental disorders, with no targeted therapeutic approaches available to date. β-glucan has been documented to regulate gut microbiota, suppress inflammation, and exert neuroprotective effects, yet its efficacy and molecular mechanisms against NEC-associated cognitive dysfunction remain unclear. title: Microbial metabolites and MAMPs: orchestrators of intestinal stem cell function.
abstract: Intestinal stem cells (ISCs) are essential for maintaining and regenerating the intestinal epithelium. abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by chronic neuroinflammation, metabolic dysfunction, and impaired proteostasis. title: Surface-functionalized Bifidobacterium bifidum alleviates Clostridioides difficile infection by coordinating host immune modulation and gut microbiota restoration☆.
abstract: Clostridioides difficile infection (CDI) is a major ecological disruption of the gut ecosystem, characterized by loss of colonization resistance, persistent inflammatory feedback and incomplete microbial recovery. abstract: The gut-muscle axis has been proposed to link gut microbiota with skeletal muscle physiology, yet its universality across livestock species remains unclear. abstract: Ischemic stroke (IS) remains a leading cause of death and long-term neurological disability worldwide, and current treatment options are constrained by narrow therapeutic windows and limited neuroprotective efficacy. abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic, disabling and incurable autoimmune disease. abstract: Streptococcus pneumoniae is a leading human respiratory pathogen, yet its success depends not on disease but on its ability to persist as an asymptomatic colonizer of the nasopharynx. abstract: Extracellular DNA (eDNA) is both a structural component of microbial biofilms and a potential reservoir of genetic information, yet its role as an ecological material remains largely unexplored.
